newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS GIVE SANDY ALOMAR TWO-YEAR EXTENSION.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS GIVE SANDY ALOMAR TWO-YEAR EXTENSION.

text.p: The Cleveland Indians on Wednesday signed four-time All-Star catcher Sandy Alomar to a two-year contract extension through 1999, with a club option for the 2000 season.
The Indians had originally decided not to pick up the $3 million option on Alomar's contract for 1998, which would have made him a free agent following the 1997 season.
But that decision was made while the club was still attempting to re-sign slugger Albert Belle, who has since signed a huge deal with the Chicago White Sox.
"We are very much looking forward to having Sandy Alomar behind the plate for us through the turn of the century," said Indians general manager John Hart.

Alomar, 30, hit .263 last year with 11 homers and 50 RBI in 127 games. He was named the American League Rookie of the Year in 1990 and owns a career .270 batting average with 53 home runs and 265 RBI.
"Sandy has been a pivotal part of the rise and success of this organisation," Hart said. "Sandy is a true leader, a hard worker and a quality person who is very deserving of this extension."
